issues.description: Method name mismatch for the farm-song operation: the problem statement (UML and task text) refers to a method named printFarmSong() (e.g., problem_statement.md: UML line and task "Implement the method printFarmSong() inside Farm.java"), while both the provided template and the reference solution define and expose a public method named singFarmSong() (signature: public void singFarmSong() in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java). Main.java in both template and solution also calls singFarmSong(). This identifier inconsistency (printFarmSong vs. singFarmSong) can confuse students about which method to implement or call and may cause mismatches with instructor tests or automated graders expecting the name from the problem statement.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the method name across all artifacts. Options: (a) Update the problem statement (UML and task text) to refer to singFarmSong() instead of printFarmSong(); or (b) rename the public method in the template and solution from singFarmSong() to printFarmSong() (and update calls in Main); or (c) add a small wrapper public method printFarmSong() in Farm that delegates to the existing singFarmSong() to preserve both names. Apply the chosen change consistently to the UML, problem text, template implementation, solution, and any example calls.
